result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers push back on decorative motion, give a short list of functional cues with durations, and list effects to skip. A is tighter. It adds a strong no-layout-shift rule and gives the owner something concrete: a live or last-updated indicator. B is longer and more spec-heavy, and its row insert/remove animation and shake on error sit slightly at odds with its own advice not to move targets under the cursor. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers reject decorative motion and propose a similar set of functional cues. A gives a duration for every cue and explains each static item in terms of speed and fatigue (e.g., looping pulses become noise by hour three), and its owner pitch is ready to use. B adds useful ideas, a 'live' indicator and a shift-long validation test, but leaves some cues without durations and lists most of its 'say no' items without reasons.
